Subject: Reserved Capacity Offer — Dedicated Activation Options

Elena / Victor,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to get a clearer view of the models you plan to put into production and the seasonal prediction windows. Attached is a short note (Novalumen_Dedicated_Offer_v3.pdf) with three distinct reservation constructs that map to your forecast brackets. High level:

- Option A — Pilot lane (Soft-floor): 16 GPUs minimum, immediate activation window, 2-week warmup credits (up to 50% of baseline throughput), ideal for model validation and early production tests. Can be scaled to burst up to 40 GPUs for short windows.

- Option B — Stepped medium (Preferred): 64 GPUs minimum, gradual ramp (month 1: 25% committed, month 3: 60%, month 6: 100%). Includes prefix caching enabled and a one-time prewarm credit (2k GPU-hours) to accelerate model load. SLA: 99.5% uptime with regional redundancy.

- Option C — Anchored slate (Throughput-first): 256 GPUs minimum, immediate full capacity activation, reserved networking lanes and priority placement. Best for customers targeting consistent heavy throughput right away.

A few clarifying notes that matter to procurement:
- Minimum billing floor applies to the committed GPUs per month; we bill based on committed units unless you consume burst capacity beyond the committed baseline.
- A phased ramp lets us keep your unit economics lower in months 1–3 while you iterate prompts.
- We offer a 90-day activation window for migration; activation milestones are documented in the attached SOW spreadsheet.

Can you share a short 6‑month consumption forecast (rough token/reqs per minute) by EOD Monday? I'll map the forecast onto the three options and include estimated month-by-month billing and cost per 1k tokens.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park

Elena — quick follow up from my side with a recommended activation pattern that enables the staggered billing Elena mentioned while preserving placement guarantees:

Recommended (variant of Option B): 64-GPU Stepped commit with staged billing floor
- Month 0 (activation): 16 GPUs committed — baseline network & KV cache warmed.
- Month 1–2: 16 GPUs billing floor, we provide a 50% useable burst allowance (up to 32 GPUs) at standard burst rate; prewarm credits applied during this window.
- Month 3: billing floor increases to 40 GPUs; prewarm credit expires at the end of month 3.
- Month 6: billing floor reaches 64 GPUs (full committed tier).

Operational details:
- Activation timeline: onboarding sprint (2 weeks), model warmup (up to 14 days using prewarm credits), canary traffic split (7–14 days) before full routing.
- Burst windows: configured as hourly slots (max 2 hours/day) and a daily flexible burst pool for unexpected runs.
- Cost anchors: attached sheet maps committed vs. burst unit rates; approximate blended rate for staged B = $X.XX / GPU-hour (detailed numbers in Drive link).

Procurement notes to include in SOW (I added to SOW-dedicated-activation.xlsx):
- Billing floor definition and measurement window.
- Convertibility: ability to convert committed GPUs to longer-term reserved units if you accelerate ramp sooner.
- Credit reconciliation: prewarm credit redemption and unused credit valuation (we propose conversion to a 30-day credit on future usage if <50% used).

Link to the detailed cost workbook: https://drive.redwood.com/novalumen/dedicated-offer-v3

If that staggered billing pattern works for you, Kimberly — we can put a pricelist and a redlined SOW into a DocuSign-ready package tomorrow.

Thanks,
